title: Unit 8 test: Applications of Integration
author: ab-4
directions: This practice test has two sections. Section I is multiple choice: Part A without a calculator and Part B with a graphing calculator. Section II is free response: Part A with a graphing calculator and Part B without one. Show your work on free-response questions; answers without supporting work may not earn full credit. Unless a question says otherwise, angles are in radians, exact answers are expected without a calculator, and calculator answers are given to three decimal places. Results are raw points for practice only.

figures.alt: Velocity–time graph of a particle for 0 ≤ t ≤ 8 seconds, with velocity in meters per second, made of straight segments joining (0, −3), (1, 0), (3, 4), (5, 4), (7, 0), and (8, −2).
The parabola y = 4 − x^2 and the line y = x + 2, which meet at (−2, 0) and (1, 3). The region R between them, with the parabola above the line, is shaded.

parts.directions: Choose the best answer. No calculator is allowed.

items.prompt: What is the average value of f(x) = 3√x on the interval [0, 4]?
items.rationale: ∫ from 0 to 4 of 3√x dx = 2x^(3/2) from 0 to 4 = 16, and 16/(4 − 0) = 4.

distractorNotes.A: 16 is the integral before dividing by the length of the interval.
distractorNotes.C: 6 is f(4), the value at the right endpoint.
distractorNotes.D: 3 averages the endpoint values f(0) = 0 and f(4) = 6.

items.prompt: A particle moves along the x-axis with velocity v(t) = 3t^2 − 6t. If the particle is at x = 4 when t = 1, where is it when t = 3?

distractorNotes.A: 2 is the displacement, without the starting position.
distractorNotes.B: Adds the total distance traveled, 6, instead of the displacement.
distractorNotes.C: 4 is the starting position; the particle does move.

items.prompt: The graph shows the velocity v(t), in meters per second, of a particle moving along a line for 0 ≤ t ≤ 8 seconds. What is the total distance the particle travels?
items.rationale: Unsigned areas: 1.5 on [0, 1], 4 on [1, 3], 8 on [3, 5], 4 on [5, 7], and 1 on [7, 8], for 18.5 m.

distractorNotes.B: 13.5 m is the displacement, where the negative areas are subtracted.
distractorNotes.C: Counts only the time the particle moves in the positive direction.
distractorNotes.D: Counts only the time the particle moves in the negative direction.

items.prompt: A tank holds 20 liters of water at time t = 0. Water flows in at a rate of 6√t liters per minute. How much water is in the tank at t = 9 minutes?

distractorNotes.A: 108 L is the water added, without the initial 20 L.
distractorNotes.B: Adds the rate at t = 9, 18 L/min, instead of accumulating it.

items.prompt: What is the area of the region bounded by y = e^x, y = e^(−x), and the line x = 1?
items.rationale: The curves meet at x = 0, and e^x is on top on [0, 1]: ∫ from 0 to 1 of (e^x − e^(−x)) dx = [e^x + e^(−x)] from 0 to 1 = e + 1/e − 2.

distractorNotes.B: Adds the curves, or uses −e^(−x) as an antiderivative of −e^(−x).
distractorNotes.C: Leaves out the value of the antiderivative at the lower limit, 2.
distractorNotes.D: Integrates the top curve only and ignores e^(−x).

items.prompt: What is the area of the region enclosed by the curves x = y^2 and x = 3 − 2y^2?
items.rationale: The curves meet where y^2 = 3 − 2y^2, at y = ±1, and x = 3 − 2y^2 is on the right: ∫ from −1 to 1 of (3 − 3y^2) dy = 6 − 2 = 4.

distractorNotes.A: 2 is the area of the half of the region with y ≥ 0.
distractorNotes.B: Integrates only the constant 3 and drops the y^2 terms.
distractorNotes.D: Doubles a symmetric integral that already covers both halves.

items.prompt: The base of a solid is the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (4, 0), and (0, 2). Cross sections perpendicular to the x-axis are equilateral triangles. What is the volume of the solid?

distractorNotes.A: 16/3 is the volume with square cross sections.
distractorNotes.C: Uses (√3/2)s^2 for the area of an equilateral triangle.
distractorNotes.D: 2π/3 is the volume with semicircular cross sections.

items.prompt: The region enclosed by y = 2√x and y = x is revolved about the x-axis. What is the volume of the solid?
items.rationale: The curves meet at x = 0 and x = 4. Washers: R = 2√x, r = x, so V = π ∫ from 0 to 4 of (4x − x^2) dx = π(32 − 64/3) = 32π/3.

distractorNotes.A: Uses π ∫ (R − r)^2 dx instead of π ∫ (R^2 − r^2) dx.
distractorNotes.B: 8/3 is the area of the region, not a volume.

parts.directions: Choose the best answer. A graphing calculator is required for some questions. If the exact value is not a choice, choose the closest approximation.

items.prompt: The graphs of y = cos(x^2) and y = x/4 cross three times for 0 < x < 3. What is the total area of the two regions enclosed by the graphs?
items.rationale: The crossings are at x ≈ 1.133, 2.308, and 2.669. The regions have areas ≈ 1.023 and ≈ 0.089, for a total ≈ 1.111.

distractorNotes.B: −0.934 is the signed integral of cos(x^2) − x/4, in which the regions cancel partly.
distractorNotes.C: 1.023 is the area of the first region only.
distractorNotes.D: 0.934 is the absolute value of the signed integral, not the total area.

items.prompt: The region between the line y = 3 and the curve y = 3 − x·e^(−x), for 0 ≤ x ≤ 4, is revolved about the line y = 3. What is the volume of the solid?
items.rationale: The region touches the axis y = 3, so the slices are discs with radius x·e^(−x): π ∫ from 0 to 4 of x^2·e^(−2x) dx ≈ 0.775.

distractorNotes.B: Revolves the region about the x-axis instead of y = 3.

items.prompt: The region under y = 1/(1 + x^2) and above the x-axis, for 0 ≤ x ≤ 2, is revolved about the x-axis. What is the volume of the solid?
A particle moves along a line with velocity v(t) = e^(sin t) − 1.5 for 0 ≤ t ≤ 5. What is the total distance the particle travels over this time?
items.rationale: Total distance = ∫ from 0 to 5 of |v(t)| dt ≈ 3.743; v changes sign at t ≈ 0.417 and t ≈ 2.724.

distractorNotes.B: 0.749 is the average speed, the distance divided by 5.
distractorNotes.D: 0.311 is the size of the displacement, not the distance.

parts.directions: A graphing calculator is required. Show the setup for every calculator result, and give answers to three decimal places with units.

items.prompt: Cars enter a parking garage at a rate modeled by E(t) = 60 + 40sin(πt/6) cars per hour and leave at a rate modeled by L(t) = 20 + 12√t cars per hour, where t is the number of hours after the garage opens, for 0 ≤ t ≤ 10. There are 120 cars in the garage at t = 0.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How many cars enter the garage during the 10 hours? Show the integral you use.

rubric.criterion: Sets up ∫ from 0 to 10 of E(t) dt.

parts.answer: ∫ from 0 to 10 of E(t) dt ≈ 638.197 cars
steps: The integral of an entry rate in cars per hour over hours gives cars.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the average rate at which cars leave the garage over 0 ≤ t ≤ 10. Include units.

rubric.criterion: Uses (1/10) ∫ from 0 to 10 of L(t) dt.

parts.answer: (1/10) ∫ from 0 to 10 of L(t) dt ≈ 45.298 cars per hour
steps: The average value of L on [0, 10] is (1/10) ∫ L(t) dt.
∫ from 0 to 10 of (20 + 12√t) dt ≈ 452.982, so the average is about 45.298 cars per hour.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: How many cars are in the garage at t = 10?

rubric.criterion: Uses 120 + ∫ from 0 to 10 of (E(t) − L(t)) dt.

steps: Amount at t = 10 = 120 + ∫ from 0 to 10 of (E(t) − L(t)) dt.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: At what time t in [0, 10] is the number of cars in the garage greatest? Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Explains that E − L changes from positive to negative there, or evaluates the candidates t = 0, 6.458, and 10.
Concludes the maximum is at t ≈ 6.458, with about 397.631 cars, more than 120 and 305.215 at the endpoints.

parts.answer: At t ≈ 6.458 hours, when there are about 397.631 cars.
steps: N′(t) = E(t) − L(t) is zero only at t ≈ 6.458 in (0, 10); it is positive before and negative after.

parts.directions: No calculator is allowed. Show your work and give exact answers.

items.prompt: Let R be the region enclosed by the graphs of y = 4 − x^2 and y = x + 2, shown in the figure.

parts.label: a

rubric.criterion: Finds the intersections x = −2 and x = 1 and writes ∫ from −2 to 1 of (2 − x − x^2) dx.

steps: 4 − x^2 = x + 2 gives x^2 + x − 2 = 0, so x = −2 and x = 1.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: The region R is the base of a solid whose cross sections perpendicular to the x-axis are squares. Find the volume of the solid.

rubric.criterion: Writes ∫ from −2 to 1 of (2 − x − x^2)^2 dx.

steps: The side of each square is the vertical length (4 − x^2) − (x + 2) = 2 − x − x^2.
(2 − x − x^2)^2 = x^4 + 2x^3 − 3x^2 − 4x + 4, and its integral from −2 to 1 is 81/10.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the volume of the solid formed when R is revolved about the line y = −1.

rubric.criterion: Uses outer radius 5 − x^2 and inner radius x + 3, both measured from y = −1.
Writes π ∫ from −2 to 1 of ((5 − x^2)^2 − (x + 3)^2) dx.

steps: From y = −1 the parabola is 4 − x^2 + 1 = 5 − x^2 away and the line is x + 2 + 1 = x + 3 away.
(5 − x^2)^2 − (x + 3)^2 = x^4 − 11x^2 − 6x + 16, whose integral from −2 to 1 is 153/5.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Write, but do not evaluate, an integral expression for the volume of the solid formed when R is revolved about the line y = 5.

rubric.criterion: Identifies outer radius 5 − (x + 2) = 3 − x and inner radius 5 − (4 − x^2) = 1 + x^2.
Writes π ∫ from −2 to 1 of ((3 − x)^2 − (1 + x^2)^2) dx.

steps: The line y = 5 lies above R, so the far boundary is the line y = x + 2 and the near boundary is the parabola.
Each radius is 5 minus the boundary's y-value.
